changes.review: PR #6: citation resolution and ibid state are output-affecting; run a full relink.
PR #5 after #6: Hebrew-numeral line markers are output-affecting; run a full relink.

PR #6 and PR #5 with the ibid checkpoint sidecar: the sidecar itself is output-neutral (an uninterrupted book sees the same history it always did; it only lets a recycled book resume instead of replaying), but the chain from the published lineage still carries PR #6's citation/ibid resolution and PR #5's line markers; run a full relink.

Otzaria/otzaria#2408: relative citations naming the citing tractate ("לקמן גיטין דף כג:") are recovered from failed resolutions, and so are untitled ones inside a Bavli tractate or its "X on <tractate>" commentary whose whole anchor is one address ("לקמן יא:", "לעיל ב,א", "לקמן צה ע\"ב", or a lone "לקמן ע\"ב" for the other amud of the citing daf), kept out of the ibid history; lines of a non-Sefaria "X על <tractate>" are placed for this by their own daf headings; output-affecting, run a full relink. Full-book planning is limited by the shared canonical Bavli-title gate, excluding Sefaria and KSK; other books retain exact per-line reuse. Otzaria/otzaria#2490: a failed citation whose parts before its one "(" only locate the address (RELATIVE, or a chapter locator such as "בריש מרובה" / "בפרק החובל") is resolved from the parenthesized title and number alone, kept out of the ibid history; a whole-daf target whose anchor is followed mid-line by ":" right after the spelled daf number becomes amud b. A failed "פרק X דמסכת דף N" (chapter before title, e.g. "בפרק שני דכתובות (דף יח:", "פ"ק דיומא דף י"ד") resolves its title and address alone and is kept only when a chapter it names, in Sefaria's own chapter terms, overlaps the result; the citation is where daf and chapter meet: a whole daf with one amud in the chapter narrows to it, and an amud written after it (":", ".", ע"א/ע"ב) outside the chapter drops the citation. A chapter phrase before a parenthesized address only narrows it the same way and never drops it, since authors use some chapter names for other chapters than Sefaria ("דיני ממונות בתרא" for "זה בורר"). A mid-line colon after spaces or HTML tags also marks amud b; the original anchor extends through that colon, while the spelled-daf and line-final-colon guards still apply. This is output-affecting and requires a full relink. Failed citations whose numbers carry a geresh after more than one letter ("תהלים יח' לא'") are rebuilt from the text when the Ref is a non-empty Tanakh ref with exactly the spelled sections, also kept out of the ibid history.
